reason: The cited evidence does not address premelting, melting, or surface disorder effects on thermal stability in HEA nanoparticles. E1 discusses synthesis methods and entropy stabilization during formation, E2 covers nucleation free energy, and E3 describes laser synthesis mechanisms, none of which provide direct support for the key mechanistic premises linking surface-to-volume ratio to depressed melting.
premises: Smaller nanoparticles have a larger surface-to-volume ratio
Surface atoms have reduced coordination and higher local disorder
Higher surface disorder/excess entropy lowers the energy barrier for atomic rearrangements
Lower energy barrier leads to depressed premelting onset and lower melting temperature
This size-dependent melting depression holds for CoCrFeMnNi HEA nanoparticles in the 5–15 nm range
